question: The engine has only ever optimized MAE. Stated as a plain accuracy - how often does it call the SIGN of the next difficulty adjustment correctly - can that percentage be raised by optimizing it directly?

headline.note: 'always guess up' scores 67.9% because difficulty rises far more often than it falls. The champion's edge over that trivial rule at k=500 is +1.8pp.

candidate: walk-forward L2 logistic regression on [extrap, mom, slope], trained on the up/down label directly

tuning_lt330.read: tuning says logistic wins ONLY at k=500; sign-of-regression wins at k=1000 and k=1500

locked_test.read: the tuning-stage ORDERING replicated at all four horizons - logistic better at k=500, worse at k=1000/1500

verdict: NOT PROVEN - improvement is within noise at n=109
interpretation: 73.4% vs the champion's 69.7% is a +3.7pp gain that cannot be distinguished from chance: the two models disagree on only 18 of 109 epochs and split them 11-7 (McNemar p=0.48).
The candidate's 95% CI [64.1%, 81.4%] still contains the trivial base rate of 67.9%, so the candidate is not even demonstrably better than always guessing 'up'.

The tuning stage DID correctly predict which model wins at which horizon in all four cases, so the k=500 ordering is not a fluke of the test split - but ordering replicating is not the same as the size of the gain being measurable.
This is a POWER limit, not an idea limit. At the observed discordance rate, demonstrating a 3.7pp gain at p<0.05 needs roughly 600 test epochs (~23 years of Bitcoin). 109 exist.

Practical consequence: at k=500 no directional forecast from headers can be shown to beat 'assume difficulty rises'. The horizons where the model has a real, significant edge are k=1000 (81.7%, p=0.004) and k=1500 (89.0%, p<0.001), and by then most of the epoch has already been observed.
delivered: dir_acc / dir_base_rate / dir_edge added to mie.evaluation.metrics.score, so every future experiment reports the accuracy percentage next to MAE, always with its baseline attached.
